Let g = gcd(a, b), and write a = gx, b = gy with gcd(x, y) = 1. The equation becomes

g²(x + y²) = 10000.

So g² divides 10000, which means g divides 100. Set N = 10000/g², so that x = N − y². We need x ≥ 1, so y² < N.

Also gcd(x, y) = gcd(N − y², y) = gcd(N, y), so the coprimality condition is gcd(y, N) = 1. For each g, we count y in [1, ⌊√(N−1)⌋] with gcd(y, N) = 1.

| g | N | range of y | condition | count |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 10000 | y ≤ 99 | coprime to 10 | 99 − 49 − 19 + 9 = 40 |
| 2 | 2500 | y ≤ 49 | coprime to 10 | 49 − 24 − 9 + 4 = 20 |
| 4 | 625 | y ≤ 24 | coprime to 5 | 24 − 4 = 20 |
| 5 | 400 | y ≤ 19 | coprime to 10 | 19 − 9 − 3 + 1 = 8 |
| 10 | 100 | y ≤ 9 | coprime to 10 | 4 |
| 20 | 25 | y ≤ 4 | coprime to 5 | 4 |
| 25 | 16 | y ≤ 3 | odd | 2 |
| 50 | 4 | y ≤ 1 | coprime to 2 | 1 |
| 100 | 1 | none | | 0 |

Total: 40 + 20 + 20 + 8 + 4 + 4 + 2 + 1 + 0 = 99.

ANSWER: 99
